title: 📈 Projects test script
who: You are Kelvin, who looks after the money at Zuri Fiber. Everything is pretend and stays on your phone — no money moves. The numbers are examples.

sessions.title: Your video, and planning a new town
sessions.intro: Watch the video, then plan a pretend new town called Kijabe: what it costs to start, what it costs each month, and how many people will pay. Zuri then says when the money comes back.

steps.do: Tap 🎓 Open practice at this screen. Turn your sound on and tap ▶ Tap to start. Watch the 📈 Projects video (9 short chapters). You can stop with ✕ at any time and come back here.
steps.see: A dark bar at the bottom speaks and shows the words, and a yellow ring points at each part of the screen. At the end of each chapter, the next one starts by itself.
steps.tip: If the voice is too fast, tap ⏸ to pause. The words are also written in the dark bar.

steps.do: Back here: tap 🎓 Open practice at this screen, then tap 🧹 Start over (pretend company) and OK — so your numbers match these steps.
steps.see: The page reloads. The Me page shows Kelvin, and the top bar says “Kelvin · Office”.

steps.do: Read the green box at the top. Then look at the two example projects.
steps.see: Suswa (example) is under 🚀 Live. Narok (example) is under 📝 Planning. Each card has one line saying how it is doing.

steps.do: Open Narok (example). Read the green line at the top, then tap “the answer ↓” and read the box “You get your … back in month …”.
steps.see: The top line says “Start-up KES 10.5M · pays back in month 24 · break-even month 8”. The answer box explains break-even, payback and the most money tied up.

steps.do: Tap ← Projects, then ＋ New project. Name: Kijabe test. Leave the area as “A new area”. Tap Create and fill in the plan.
steps.see: A new project page for “Kijabe test”. The green line at the top says “Start-up KES 0”.

steps.do: In 🏗️ A · Start-up costs type: Fiber cable to lay 4 · Fiber cost per km 290000 · OLT & core equipment 600000 · Labour 350000.
steps.see: Next to “A · Start-up costs” it says KES 2.3M. (Zuri adds 10% extra for surprises — that is the Contingency box.)

steps.do: Tap 🔁 B · Running costs to open it. Backhaul quote: choose “Bayobab 100 Mbps”. Staff 2 · Salary each 22000 · Rent 10000.
steps.see: Next to “B · Running costs” it says KES 68k/mo.

steps.do: Tap 💰 C · Customers & money in. Homes & businesses passed 700. Sign-ups by month 1: 15 · month 3: 40 · month 6: 80 · month 12: 140 · month 24: 220. Install fee 2500. Customers who leave each month 2. Then tap Use it next to “From Zuri A today”.
steps.see: The monthly bill fills in from Zuri A (KES 2,647). A line says about how many customers you will really have. The green line at the top now says “pays back in month 14”.

steps.do: Scroll down to “What if?”. Read the row “Low (70%)” — that is if only 70 of every 100 expected people join.
steps.see: Nine boxes with month numbers (or “never”). The bold box in the middle is your plan: m 14.

sessions.title: Compare, share, and decide
sessions.intro: Put the towns side by side, try a loan, share a plan, and say “we're doing it” — which needs a second person's OK.

steps.do: Read the table. Which town gives the money back sooner?
steps.see: Kijabe test, Suswa (example) and Narok (example) side by side. The quickest Payback has a ⭐ (Kijabe test, month 14).

steps.do: Open Narok (example). Tap 🏦 D · A loan? Untick “Include a loan” and look at the boxes under “The answer”. Then tick it again.
steps.see: With the loan ticked, the Start-up box says “loan 5.0M · yours 5.5M” — the partners only put in 5.5M of their own money.

steps.do: Scroll to “Share with the partners”. Tap 📋 Copy for WhatsApp. (Paste it in a note on your phone to read it — not to a real group.) Then tap 🖨 One-page report.
steps.see: “Copied” at the bottom of the screen. Then a clean page: “Zuri Fiber — Narok (example): should we build it?” with numbered parts and “Questions to agree on”.

steps.do: Open Narok (example) again. At “The decision”, tap ✅ We're doing it. Keep the launch month and tap Send for the second OK.
steps.see: An orange box: “⏳ Waiting for a second OK”. There is no Approve button for you — someone else must approve. The numbers are now locked (grey).

steps.do: Tap 🎭 Practice: switch to Jerry to approve. Then tap ✅ Approve — lock the plan.
steps.see: The page now shows “📊 Actual vs plan” for Narok and “🚀 Approved — starts …”. The plan is kept as the yardstick.

sessions.title: Following the real results
sessions.intro: Suswa started 5 months ago. See how it is really doing against the plan, fill in last month, change what you now expect, and find it in the Friday report.

steps.do: Open Suswa (example). Read the coloured box at the top.
steps.see: 🟠 Behind plan: “After 5 months, Suswa (example) has KES 273,179 less cash than the plan expected”, and “you get your money back in month 28 … the plan said month 25”.

steps.do: Tap the orange line “… aren't confirmed yet”. Customers: keep 86 and tap Save. Then Money collected: keep 163800 and tap Save.
steps.see: The orange line goes away. In the table, the last month no longer has a “?”.

steps.do: Tap ＋ Record actuals. What: Running costs paid. Which line: Power / generator fuel. Amount 7500. Note: My test entry. Tap Save.
steps.see: “My test entry” is at the top of the Actuals list, with Running costs paid · Power / generator fuel.

steps.do: Open 📝 Forecast. Tap 💰 C, change Average monthly bill to 1700. Tap 💾 Save the forecast…, write why: Test: customers chose the cheaper package. Tap Save the forecast. Then open 📜 Log.
steps.see: The Log shows “📝 Forecast updated” with your words, and the change “Monthly bill (ARPU): 1,800 → 1,700”.
steps.copy: Test: customers chose the cheaper package
auto: Test: customers chose the cheaper package
Test: customers chose the cheaper package

steps.do: Go to Home. Find the “📈 Projects:” card. Then open Money → 📊 Report and find “📈 Projects” in the report text.
steps.see: Home: one line — Suswa (example) behind plan · Narok (example) starts … · Kijabe test being planned. The Friday report has one line for each project.
